=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

## Preliminary point: the [STANDARD] labels

The Seller's note asks us to treat items marked [STANDARD] as agreed and to review only [OPEN] items. I have not done that. Nothing in the file shows the Buyer agreed to these positions, and several [STANDARD] items are among the Buyer's largest exposures (SPA-N-001, -003, -006, -007, -014). Every item below is reviewed on its merits. We also have only the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA, so clause references follow the Seller's own numbering.

## Known exposures (for context)

| Item | Amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility outstanding | ~AUD 3.2m | DD-003 |
| Employee Completion bonuses (excl. on-costs) | AUD 420k | DD-005 |
| Ironquay SOW3 fees open | AUD 180k | DD-010 |
| Sandbar renewals | AUD 330k | DD-008, DD-011 |
| **Subtotal, quantified** | **~AUD 4.13m** | |
| Bluefen revenue at risk (~30% of revenue, not a liability) | ~AUD 3.6m FY26 | DD-002 |

The Seller's proposed 20% general cap (AUD 4.8m) is only about AUD 0.7m above the quantified items. If these known matters are left to general warranty claims, they will erode the cap. They should be dealt with through price adjustment, funds flow and specific indemnities, not general warranties.

---

## Liability and claims mechanics

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A general cap of 30% (AUD 7.2m), with fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud carved out and capped at price or uncapped as appropriate.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. 20% is within market, but only if known matters are removed from the warranty pool.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** A tipping basket (once exceeded, the whole loss is recoverable from the first dollar); a lower de minimis (around AUD 10k); related claims aggregated for both thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. A deductible basket of this size, combined with a de minimis that excludes claims from the basket count, significantly reduces recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** General claims notified within 18 months of Completion; the limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** General warranties at 24 months; fundamental and tax claims at 6 years (or the statutory period plus a margin); a requirement to commence proceedings within a set period after notice.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The "applies to all unless stated" drafting puts the default in the Seller's favour.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, outside the basket and de minimis, with a 6-year survival period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title failure goes to the core of the 100% share acquisition and should not be treated as an ordinary warranty claim.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. The limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature," which would include fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that fraud, and fraudulent concealment, by the Seller or Company is uncapped, not subject to time limits, and not barred by the exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clauses.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted and insert an express carve-out. Relying on general law to limit contractual protection is not sufficient for a deal of this size.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only. Data room documents should be disclosed only where specifically referred to, and only against a fair-disclosure standard. Public register disclosure should not qualify warranties in general terms.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A whole-room disclosure would largely neutralise the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Pro-sandbagging wording (Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice warranty claims). In any case, specific indemnities for known matters must apply regardless of knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The clause would bar claims on exactly the matters the Buyer has identified, which are the ones it most needs to be protected against.

---

## Conditions and specific matters

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Final consent and evidence of conditions (cl 11.2/11.3) not yet provided.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen written consent, with any conditions in cl 11.3 satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. A Buyer termination right if not obtained by a long-stop date. A specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen relationship if the consent is obtained on conditions the Seller has not satisfied.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "reasonable endeavours." Make it a hard condition precedent, since ~30% of revenue depends on it.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** Payout of the facility from the price at Completion (consistent with the debt-free basis), with a payout letter from Riverlark and discharge of security delivered at Completion or held in escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. On a debt-free basis the Buyer should not be funding debt it has not priced.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Matter for the Seller; not itemised in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420k plus all employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and any other employer liabilities) treated as debt-like items deducted from price. Seller to bear any amounts that fall due after Completion where the bonus relates to pre-Completion service or the Completion event. A specific indemnity for any unpaid bonus claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the funds flow exclusion. These are Completion-linked liabilities and must be reflected in price.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; described as "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** A full specific indemnity covering any defect in ownership of Project Materials, third-party IP claims, and costs of obtaining a confirmatory assignment. Payment of the AUD 180k SOW3 balance (or a retention) and a confirmatory assignment delivered as conditions to Completion. The indemnity should sit outside the basket and cap, or be capped at a separate amount.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay agreement makes transfer of Project Materials conditional on payment, and no payment receipt or assignment is in the data room.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** A forensic report and legal assessment before signing, including whether this is an eligible data breach under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), with timing of any assessment checked urgently. A specific indemnity covering notification costs, regulatory action, customer claims and remediation, backed by escrow or retention. A specific warranty that no notifiable breach has occurred, or disclosure of the one that has.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation. ~1,240 records containing personal information, with unknown access, cannot be treated as immaterial. Specialist privacy advice is needed.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330k aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The contracts produced, with term, termination rights, pricing and whether they were entered into outside the ordinary course. Confirmation that the three renewals are not one arrangement split to fall under review thresholds. If the terms are unfavourable or non-terminable beyond Completion, treat as price adjustment or Seller cost.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. The "ordinary course" label cannot be accepted until the contracts are reviewed.

---

## Structure, verification and tax/IP

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all claims of any nature.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties (title, capacity), tax, specific indemnities and fraud, each with its own cap, threshold, time limit and disclosure treatment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A single regime makes the fundamental and tax protections meaningless.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, certified copy of the register, executed transfer forms, PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no options or other share issues, review of constitution transfer restrictions, and a title warranty backed by the fundamental regime above.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. A register supplied by the Seller is evidence of the Seller's position, not independent verification of title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (including payroll tax, GST, income tax and superannuation) outside the basket and general cap, with a survival period of at least 6 years. Tax warranties. IP warranties covering ownership of core IP, non-infringement and the Ironquay materials. Pre-Completion tax liabilities identified in due diligence treated as debt-like items in the price.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Tax and IP are not settled, and the general regime (with its cap, basket and 18-month limit) is unsuitable for them.

---

## Priority actions

1. **Reject the [STANDARD] framing** and confirm to the Seller in writing that no item is agreed until the Buyer has completed its mark-up.
2. **Move known matters out of the warranty pool**: Riverlark payout, bonuses and on-costs, Ironquay SOW3 payment, and Sandbar terms, dealt with through funds flow and price.
3. **Make Bluefen consent and the Ironquay assignment conditions precedent.**
4. **Commission the export incident assessment now**, given the NDB timing.
5. **Insert the fraud carve-out, category separation and pro-sandbagging wording** into the SPA mark-up.
6. **Have NSW corporate, tax and privacy specialists confirm** the treatment of the bonuses, payroll tax, superannuation and the notification analysis before the mark-up goes out.
